primary_goal: Identify the exact background music playing during the broadcast represented by the supplied CRT-TV photograph.

source_asset.hard_constraint: The still image carries no audio fingerprint. Exact soundtrack identification requires a frame-matched archival recording or an audio/video sample from the source footage.

visual_fingerprint.format: 4:3 SD-era Call-TV presentation photographed from a CRT
features: male presenter in a small panel at left
two near-identical photographs side-by-side in the main field
woman and dog visible in both comparison images
mass-calling telephone information in the lower third
visual_fingerprint.presenter_visual_only: The male presenter visible in the supplied still appears to have relatively short/dark hair. This is only a visual descriptor for cross-matching broadcasts; no identity inference is made.

broadcast_attribution.best_current_attribution: 9Live production ecosystem: either 9Live itself or a 9Live-produced Call-TV window on another ProSiebenSat.1-family channel
broadcast_attribution.caveat: No clearly readable station bug is visible in the supplied still, so production identity must not be conflated with broadcast-channel identity.

likely_phone_number.note: CRT moire prevents treating every photographed digit as independently resolved; historical 9Live sources strongly corroborate this canonical number.

major_new_evidence.reported_broadcast_reference: 17.10, approximately 23:28 as written by the requester
major_new_evidence.reported_music_behavior: The requester said the same track played repeatedly as an endless/background loop in that 9Live quiz show.
major_new_evidence.show_descriptor: The requester explicitly described that quiz show as having a long-haired blond male presenter.
major_new_evidence.sample_resolution: On 2004-12-16, after posting a sample, the requester reported the identification as Brainbug - Nightmare (Burger Queens Remix).
major_new_evidence.reason_for_downrank_from_v1_0: The textual presenter description in the 2004 music thread does not visually fit the presenter in the supplied still. This strongly suggests Brainbug is a proven 9Live-era background track from another quiz-show instance rather than proof of this exact frame's soundtrack.

second_documented_era_track.evidence: A contemporary fan report states that 9Live was playing Reality as background music. Follow-up discussion indicates multiple tracks from an Altromondo compilation were also heard on 9Live.

playlist_behavior.finding: 9Live did not appear to use one universal background theme.
playlist_behavior.evidence: In a 2006 viewer inquiry reproduced online, the 9Live viewer editorial office stated that it did not list the music titles and that there was no general playlist.
playlist_behavior.implication: Music identification must be tied to the exact show/time or recovered audio, not merely to the channel.

pressure_cue_behavior.finding: Music was also used dynamically as a Call-TV urgency cue.
pressure_cue_behavior.evidence: Contemporary descriptions document dramatic music and ticking before caller connection; a 2004 discussion also describes presenters signaling an approaching end through music changes.
pressure_cue_behavior.implication: A single broadcast could contain several background/cue tracks, further weakening any channel-wide one-track assumption.

pass_conditions: Locate archival video containing the exact woman-and-dog Fehlerbild with the same 1,000 EUR graphic package and inspect its soundtrack.
OR obtain approximately 5-15 seconds of audio/video from the source recording and compare/fingerprint it against candidate tracks and broader music databases.
exact_identification_gate.prohibited_inference: Do not promote an era-compatible 9Live track to exact soundtrack identification without frame-level archival or audio-level evidence.

epistemic_verdict.confidence_policy: Evidence beats resemblance; silence or absence of an indexed archive match is not negative proof.
